{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3328abc2c50a563d6b374c06346f2aa5d559bf69e1b7a38ca2118eea15b27168","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Equipment, defensive-driving and wireless-device confusables","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: mirror and horn distances, flashers, muffler and emissions, attitudes, beginners and experienced drivers, the phone law, steering","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: mirror and horn distances, flashers, muffler and emissions, attitudes, beginners and experienced drivers, the phone law, steering
Look-alike rules from the equipment and safe-driving pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
The required outside mirror must show 200 feet of road behind, and the required horn must be audible at 200 feet, so one distance covers both rules. [A01]
Why it matters: group equipment; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F10 versus sec05-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
Hazard flashers are switched on when you are stopped on the roadway or shoulder, while flashing red lights facing forward are off-limits to ordinary vehicles even when they break down. [A01]
Why it matters: group lights; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F13 versus sec05-F14.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
The muffler rule targets noise and pollution and bans bypass devices, while the emissions rule requires an exhaust emissions system on 1967 and newer models. [A01]
Why it matters: group emissions; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F04 versus sec05-F06.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
A head restraint lines up with the middle of the ear and touches the back of the head; it is not set to the top of the head or left low at the neck. [A01]
Why it matters: group seating; difficulty one; prereq sec05-F02.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A01
The manual gives no tint numbers; it says only that tint is lawful within limits and puts the burden on the owner to check that the installer complied. [A01]
Why it matters: group equipment; difficulty two; prereq sec05-F09.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A02
Courtesy and consideration are ranked as the most important attitudes, while concentration and alertness are described as other important elements. [A02]
Why it matters: group attitude; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F18 versus sec05-F19.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A02
Foresight is about sizing up a situation fast and being ready to correct, while defensive driving is the wider practice of awareness, planning, anticipation and right action. [A02]
Why it matters: group defensive driving; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F21 versus sec05-F16.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A02
Beginner practice in an open lot comes after the instruction permit is issued, not before it. [A02]
Why it matters: group practice; difficulty one; prereq sec05-F26.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A03
The risk the manual names for experienced drivers is carelessness, overconfidence and old bad habits, not a lack of basic skill. [A03]
Why it matters: group experience; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F27 versus sec05-F25.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A03
Holding or supporting a device is what the law bans, while hands-free and voice-to-text operation stays allowed. [A03]
Why it matters: group wireless devices; difficulty three; confusable sec05-F34 versus sec05-F37.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A03
Reporting an emergency is the single reason given for using a wireless device while driving; ordinary calls and texts mean pulling off the road and stopping first. [A03]
Why it matters: group wireless devices; difficulty three; confusable sec05-F36 versus sec05-F32.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A03
Fastening a safety belt is on the distraction list only when it is done while driving, so the belt goes on before the vehicle moves. [A03]
Why it matters: group distractions; difficulty one; prereq sec05-F31.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A03
On a straight road you look well ahead and make slight corrections, while in a curve you look toward the outside of your lane. [A03]
Why it matters: group steering; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F38 versus sec05-F39.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]
